sanskrit: ekonatriṃśe divase yaḥ prāśed ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsān vai satyavrataparāyaṇaḥ
english: He who on the twenty-ninth day takes but a single meal, doing so steadily for twelve months, devoted to the vow of truth—

sanskrit: tasya lokāḥ śubhā divyā devarājarṣipūjitāḥ vimānaṃ candraśubhrābhaṃ divyaṃ samadhigacchati
english: his are auspicious, celestial worlds honored by the king of the gods and by royal seers, and he attains a divine chariot radiant with the brightness of the moon.

sanskrit: jātarūpamayaṃ yuktaṃ sarvaratnavibhūṣitam apsarogaṇasaṃpūrṇaṃ gandharvair abhināditam
english: Wrought of gold, well fashioned, adorned with every jewel, thronged with hosts of apsarases and resounding with the music of gandharvas.

sanskrit: tatra cainaṃ śubhā nāryo divyābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ manobhirāmā madhurā ramayanti madotkaṭāḥ
english: There lovely women decked in divine ornaments, ravishing the mind, sweet and flushed with ardor, give him their delight.

sanskrit: bhogavāṃs tejasā yukto vaiśvānarasamaprabhaḥ divyo divyena vapuṣā bhrājamāna ivāmaraḥ
english: Rich in enjoyment, endowed with splendor, bright as the all-consuming fire, he is divine, shining in a divine form like an immortal.

sanskrit: vasūnāṃ marutāṃ caiva sādhyānām aśvinos tathā rudrāṇāṃ ca tathā lokān brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: He attains the worlds of the Vasus and the Maruts, of the Sādhyas and the two Aśvins, of the Rudras as well, and reaches the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: yas tu māse gate bhuṅkte ekabhaktaṃ śamātmakaḥ sadā dvādaśa māsān vai brahmalokam avāpnuyāt
english: But he who, when a month has passed, eats a single meal, his nature given to tranquility, doing so for twelve months, shall win the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: sudhārasakṛtāhāraḥ śrīmān sarvamanoharaḥ tejasā vapuṣā lakṣmyā bhrājate raśmivān iva
english: Taking nectar's essence for his food, glorious and altogether enchanting, he shines with splendor, with beauty, and with majesty, like the radiant sun.

sanskrit: divyamālyāmbaradharo divyagandhānulepanaḥ sukheṣv abhirato yogī duḥkhānām avijānakaḥ
english: Wearing celestial garlands and raiment, anointed with celestial fragrances, the yogin delights in pleasures and knows nothing of sorrows.

sanskrit: svayaṃprabhābhir nārībhir vimānastho mahīyate rudradevarṣikanyābhiḥ satataṃ cābhipūjyate
english: Seated in his chariot he is exalted by women luminous of themselves, and is forever worshipped by the daughters of the Rudras and the divine seers.

sanskrit: nānāvidhasurūpābhir nānārāgābhir eva ca nānāmadhurabhāṣābhir nānāratibhir eva ca
english: By women fair in manifold forms, of manifold passions, of manifold sweet speech, and of manifold delights.

sanskrit: vimāne nagarākāre sūryavat sūryasaṃnibhe pṛṣṭhataḥ somasaṃkāśe udak caivābhrasaṃnibhe
english: In a chariot vast as a city, blazing like the sun and resembling the sun, behind glowing like the moon, and on its northern side like a cloud.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāyāṃ tu raktābhe adhastān nīlamaṇḍale ūrdhvaṃ citrābhisaṃkāśe naiko vasati pūjitaḥ
english: Red-hued on its southern side, with a dark orb below and a many-colored brilliance above—there he dwells, honored and never alone.

sanskrit: yāvad varṣasahasraṃ tu jambūdvīpe pravarṣati tāvat saṃvatsarāḥ proktā brahmalokasya dhīmataḥ
english: For as many years as the rain pours down upon Jambūdvīpa through a thousand years, so long, they say, is his sojourn in the world of the wise Brahmā.

sanskrit: vipruṣaś caiva yāvantyo nipatanti nabhastalāt varṣāsu varṣatas tāvan nivasaty amaraprabhaḥ
english: And for as many raindrops as fall from the vault of heaven in the season when it rains, so long does that one, splendid as an immortal, abide there.

sanskrit: māsopavāsī varṣais tu daśabhiḥ svargam uttamam maharṣitvam athāsādya saśarīragatir bhavet
english: He who fasts for a month at a time, after ten years attains the highest heaven, and gaining the rank of a great seer, passes thither in his very body.

sanskrit: munir dānto jitakrodho jitaśiśnodaraḥ sadā juhvann agnīṃś ca niyataḥ saṃdhyopāsanasevitā
english: A sage, self-controlled, having conquered anger, having mastered the appetites of sex and belly, ever offering oblations to the fires, restrained, and faithful to worship at the twilight hours.

sanskrit: bahubhir niyamair evaṃ māsān aśnāti yo naraḥ abhrāvakāśaśīlaś ca tasya vāso nirucyate
english: The man who thus, through many observances, takes his food but once a month and lives content under the open sky—of him such a dwelling is declared.

sanskrit: divaṃ gatvā śarīreṇa svena rājan yathāmaraḥ svargaṃ puṇyaṃ yathākāmam upabhuṅkte yathāvidhi
english: Having gone to heaven in his own body, O king, like an immortal, he enjoys the holy heaven at will, according to the ordinance.

sanskrit: eṣa te bharataśreṣṭha yajñānāṃ vidhir uttamaḥ vyākhyāto hy ānupūrvyeṇa upavāsaphalātmakaḥ
english: This, O best of the Bhāratas, is the supreme ordinance of sacrifices, expounded to you in due order, which yields the fruit of fasting.

sanskrit: daridrair manujaiḥ pārtha prāpyaṃ yajñaphalaṃ yathā upavāsam imaṃ kṛtvā gacchec ca paramāṃ gatim devadvijātipūjāyāṃ rato bharatasattama
english: Thus, O Pārtha, the fruit of sacrifice may be won even by men of no means; by performing this fast one shall attain the supreme goal, O best of the Bhāratas, if he delights in the worship of gods and of the twice-born.

sanskrit: upavāsavidhis tv eṣa vistareṇa prakīrtitaḥ niyateṣv apramatteṣu śaucavatsu mahātmasu
english: This ordinance of fasting has been proclaimed at length, ordained for the restrained, the vigilant, the pure, the great of soul,

sanskrit: dambhadrohanivṛtteṣu kṛtabuddhiṣu bhārata acaleṣv aprakampeṣu mā te bhūd atra saṃśayaḥ
english: for those who have turned from deceit and malice, whose minds are made up, O Bhārata, who are steadfast and unshaken—let no doubt of yours linger here.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yad varaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ tad bravīhi pitāmaha yatra vai paramaṃ śaucaṃ tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Which is the best of all sacred bathing-places, O grandsire—tell me that; where the highest purity lies, that you ought to expound to me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sarvāṇi khalu tīrthāni guṇavanti manīṣiṇām yat tu tīrthaṃ ca śaucaṃ ca tan me śṛṇu samāhitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: All sacred fords, indeed, hold virtue for the wise; but what is the true ford and what is purity, hear from me with attentive mind.

sanskrit: agādhe vimale śuddhe satyatoye dhṛtihrade snātavyaṃ mānase tīrthe sattvam ālambya śāśvatam
english: In the fathomless, stainless, pure ford of the mind, whose waters are truth and whose pool is steadfastness, one must bathe, taking hold of the eternal goodness.

sanskrit: tīrthaśaucam anarthitvamārdavaṃ satyam ārjavam ahiṃsā sarvabhūtānām ānṛśaṃsyaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ
english: The purity of the ford is freedom from greed, gentleness, truth, uprightness, harmlessness toward all beings, mercy, self-restraint, and tranquility.

sanskrit: nirmamā nirahaṃkārā nirdvaṃdvā niṣparigrahāḥ śucayas tīrthabhūtās te ye bhaikṣam upabhuñjate
english: They who are free from the sense of mine, free from egoism, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from possessions, and who live upon alms—those are pure and are themselves as sacred fords.

sanskrit: tattvavit tv anahaṃbuddhis tīrthaṃ paramam ucyate śaucalakṣaṇam etat te sarvatraivānvavekṣaṇam
english: He who knows the truth and is free from the notion of "I" is called the supreme ford; this is the mark of purity for you, to be watched for in all things everywhere.

sanskrit: rajas tamaḥ sattvam atho yeṣāṃ nirdhautam ātmanaḥ śaucāśauce na te saktāḥ svakāryaparimārgiṇaḥ
english: They from whose self passion, darkness, and even goodness have been washed clean—such men, intent on their own true task, are not bound by the pure and the impure.

sanskrit: sarvatyāgeṣv abhiratāḥ sarvajñāḥ sarvadarśinaḥ śaucena vṛttaśaucārthās te tīrthāḥ śucayaś ca te
english: Delighting in every renunciation, all-knowing, all-seeing, having achieved purity of conduct through purity itself—those are sacred fords, and those are the pure.

sanskrit: nodakaklinnagātras tu snāta ity abhidhīyate sa snāto yo damasnātaḥ sabāhyābhyantaraḥ śuciḥ
english: Not he whose limbs are merely wet with water is called bathed; he is the truly bathed who has bathed in self-restraint and is pure both without and within.

sanskrit: atīteṣv anapekṣā ye prāpteṣv artheṣu nirmamāḥ śaucam eva paraṃ teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ notpadyate spṛhā
english: They who care nothing for what is past and claim no ownership in the goods that have come to them—theirs is the highest purity, in whom no craving arises.

sanskrit: prajñānaṃ śaucam eveha śarīrasya viśeṣataḥ tathā niṣkiṃcanatvaṃ ca manasaś ca prasannatā
english: Wisdom is purity here, especially of the body; so too are utter possessionlessness and serenity of mind.

sanskrit: vṛttaśaucaṃ manaḥśaucaṃ tīrthaśaucaṃ paraṃ hitam jñānotpannaṃ ca yac chaucaṃ tac chaucaṃ paramaṃ matam
english: Purity of conduct, purity of mind, the purity of the ford—a supreme blessing; but the purity born of knowledge, that is held to be the highest purity of all.

sanskrit: manasātha pradīpena brahmajñānabalena ca snātā ye mānase tīrthe tajjñāḥ kṣetrajñadarśinaḥ
english: They who have bathed in the ford of the mind, by the lamp of the mind and the strength of the knowledge of Brahman—those knowers behold the Knower of the field.

sanskrit: samāropitaśaucas tu nityaṃ bhāvasamanvitaḥ kevalaṃ guṇasaṃpannaḥ śucir eva naraḥ sadā
english: But the man in whom purity is established, ever endowed with right disposition, perfect in virtue alone, is forever pure indeed.

sanskrit: śarīrasthāni tīrthāni proktāny etāni bhārata pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni puṇyāni śṛṇu tāny api
english: These sacred fords that dwell within the body have been declared, O Bhārata; now hear also of the holy fords that are upon the earth.

sanskrit: yathā śarīrasyoddeśāḥ śucayaḥ parinirmitāḥ tathā pṛthivyā bhāgāś ca puṇyāni salilāni ca
english: As certain regions of the body are fashioned pure, so too are there holy tracts of the earth and holy waters.

sanskrit: prārthanāc caiva tīrthasya snānāc ca pitṛtarpaṇāt dhunanti pāpaṃ tīrtheṣu pūtā yānti divaṃ sukham
english: By yearning for the sacred ford, by bathing there, and by the offering of water to the ancestors, men shake off their sin at the fords and, purified, go in bliss to heaven.

sanskrit: parigrahāc ca sādhūnāṃ pṛthivyāś caiva tejasā atīva puṇyās te bhāgāḥ salilasya ca tejasā
english: Through the resort of holy men, through the power of the earth, and through the power of the water, those tracts become exceedingly holy.

sanskrit: manasaś ca pṛthivyāś ca puṇyatīrthās tathāpare ubhayor eva yaḥ snātaḥ sa siddhiṃ śīghram āpnuyāt
english: There are holy fords of the mind and of the earth alike; and he who has bathed in both shall swiftly attain perfection.

sanskrit: yathā balaṃ kriyāhīnaṃ kriyā vā balavarjitā neha sādhayate kāryaṃ samāyuktas tu sidhyati
english: As strength without action, or action without strength, accomplishes nothing here, but joined together they succeed—

sanskrit: evaṃ śarīraśaucena tīrthaśaucena cānvitaḥ tataḥ siddhim avāpnoti dvividhaṃ śaucam uttamam
english: so the man endowed with purity of body and with purity of the ford thereby attains perfection; the twofold purity is supreme.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaha mahābāho sarvaśāstraviśārada śrotum icchāmi martyānāṃ saṃsāravidhim uttamam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O grandsire, mighty-armed, learned in all the scriptures, I wish to hear the supreme law of the round of births and deaths for mortals.

sanskrit: kena vṛttena rājendra vartamānā narā yudhi prāpnuvanty uttamaṃ svargaṃ kathaṃ ca narakaṃ nṛpa
english: By what conduct, O lord of kings, do men who live in the world attain the highest heaven, and how, O king, do they come to hell?

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ śarīram utsṛjya kāṣṭhaloṣṭasamaṃ janāḥ prayānty amuṃ lokam itaḥ ko vai tān anugacchati
english: Casting off the dead body, like a log or a clod of earth, people pass from here to that other world; who, then, follows after them?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca asāv āyāti bhagavān bṛhaspatir udāradhīḥ pṛcchainaṃ sumahābhāgam etad guhyaṃ sanātanam
english: Bhīṣma said: Yonder comes the lord Bṛhaspati, of noble understanding; ask him, that most blessed one, of this eternal mystery.

sanskrit: naitad anyena śakyaṃ hi vaktuṃ kena cid adya vai vaktā bṛhaspatisamo na hy anyo vidyate kva cit
english: For this cannot be told by any other man today; nowhere is there found another expounder equal to Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tayoḥ saṃvadator evaṃ pārthagāṅgeyayos tadā ājagāma viśuddhātmā bhagavān sa bṛhaspatiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As the son of Pṛthā and the son of Gaṅgā were thus conversing, the lord Bṛhaspati of utterly pure soul came near.

sanskrit: tato rājā samutthāya dhṛtarāṣṭrapurogamaḥ pūjām anupamāṃ cakre sarve te ca sabhāsadaḥ
english: Then the king, with Dhṛtarāṣṭra at their head, rose up, and all those seated in the assembly paid him honor beyond compare.

sanskrit: tato dharmasuto rājā bhagavantaṃ bṛhaspatim upagamya yathānyāyaṃ praśnaṃ papraccha suvrataḥ
english: Then the king, the son of Dharma, true to his vows, drew near to the lord Bṛhaspati and, in due form, put his question.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhagavan sarvadharmajña sarvaśāstraviśārada martyasya kaḥ sahāyo vai pitā mātā suto guruḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O lord, knower of all duties, learned in all the scriptures, who is the mortal's true companion—father, mother, son, or teacher?

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ śarīram utsṛjya kāṣṭhaloṣṭasamaṃ janāḥ gacchanty amutralokaṃ vai ka enam anugacchati
english: Casting off the dead body, like a log or a clod of earth, people go to that world beyond; who, then, follows him?

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca ekaḥ prasūto rājendra jantur eko vinaśyati ekas tarati durgāṇi gacchaty ekaś ca durgatim
english: Bṛhaspati said: Alone the creature is born, O lord of kings, and alone it perishes; alone it crosses the hard passages, and alone it goes to its evil plight.

sanskrit: asahāyaḥ pitā mātā tathā bhrātā suto guruḥ jñātisaṃbandhivargaś ca mitravargas tathaiva ca
english: No helpmate then is father or mother, brother, son, or teacher, nor the throng of kinsmen and connections, nor the company of friends.

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ śarīram utsṛjya kāṣṭhaloṣṭasamaṃ janāḥ muhūrtam upatiṣṭhanti tato yānti parāṅmukhāḥ tais tac charīram utsṛṣṭaṃ dharma eko 'nugacchati
english: When the body lies dead, like a log or a clod of earth, people stand by it for a moment, then turn their faces away and depart; once that body is forsaken by them, righteousness alone follows after.

sanskrit: tasmād dharmaḥ sahāyārthe sevitavyaḥ sadā nṛbhiḥ prāṇī dharmasamāyukto gacchate svargatiṃ parām tathaivādharmasaṃyukto narakāyopapadyate
english: Therefore men must ever cultivate righteousness for the sake of a companion; the living being joined with righteousness goes to the supreme path of heaven, and joined with unrighteousness he comes to hell.

sanskrit: tasmān nyāyāgatair arthair dharmaṃ seveta paṇḍitaḥ dharma eko manuṣyāṇāṃ sahāyaḥ pāralaukikaḥ
english: Therefore let the wise man practice righteousness with wealth honestly gotten; righteousness alone is the companion of men in the world beyond.

sanskrit: lobhān mohād anukrośād bhayād vāpy abahuśrutaḥ naraḥ karoty akāryāṇi parārthe lobhamohitaḥ
english: Out of greed, delusion, misplaced pity, or fear, the man of little learning, bewildered by greed, does deeds that ought not to be done for another's sake.

sanskrit: dharmaś cārthaś ca kāmaś ca tritayaṃ jīvite phalam etat trayam avāptavyam adharmaparivarjitam
english: Duty, wealth, and pleasure—this triad is the fruit of life; this triad is to be attained while shunning all unrighteousness.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śrutaṃ bhagavato vākyaṃ dharmayuktaṃ paraṃ hitam śarīravicayaṃ jñātuṃ buddhis tu mama jāyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have heard the lord's words, righteous and supremely beneficial; now there arises in me the wish to understand the analysis of the body.

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ śarīrarahitaṃ sūkṣmam avyaktatāṃ gatam acakṣurviṣayaṃ prāptaṃ kathaṃ dharmo 'nugacchati
english: When the dead one is bereft of the body, has grown subtle, passed into the unmanifest, and become no object for the eye, how does righteousness follow after it?

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam buddhir ātmā ca sahitā dharmaṃ paśyanti nityadā
english: Bṛhaspati said: Earth, air, ether, water, and light as the fifth, together with the intellect and the self, behold righteousness without ceasing.

sanskrit: prāṇinām iha sarveṣāṃ sākṣibhūtāni cāniśam etaiś ca sa ha dharmo 'pi taṃ jīvam anugacchati
english: For all living beings here these are unceasing witnesses, and through these does righteousness itself follow after that living soul.

sanskrit: tvagasthimāṃsaṃ śukraṃ ca śoṇitaṃ ca mahāmate śarīraṃ varjayanty ete jīvitena vivarjitam
english: Skin, bone, flesh, semen, and blood, O greatly wise one—these forsake the body once it is bereft of life.

sanskrit: tato dharmasamāyuktaḥ sa jīvaḥ sukham edhate iha loke pare caiva kiṃ bhūyaḥ kathayāmi te
english: Then that living soul, joined with righteousness, thrives in happiness both in this world and in the next. What more shall I tell you?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca anudarśitaṃ bhagavatā yathā dharmo 'nugacchati etat tu jñātum icchāmi kathaṃ retaḥ pravartate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The lord has shown how righteousness follows after; but this I wish to learn—how does the seed come forth?

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca annam aśnanti ye devāḥ śarīrasthā nareśvara pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotir manas tathā
english: Bṛhaspati said: The deities that dwell within the body and consume the food, O ruler of men, are earth, air, ether, water, light, and likewise the mind.

sanskrit: tatas tṛpteṣu rājendra teṣu bhūteṣu pañcasu manaḥṣaṣṭheṣu śuddhātman retaḥ saṃpadyate mahat
english: Then, O lord of kings, when those five elements with the mind for a sixth are satisfied, O pure-souled one, the abundant seed is formed.

sanskrit: tato garbhaḥ saṃbhavati strīpuṃsoḥ pārtha saṃgame etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: Thereupon, at the union of woman and man, O Pārtha, the embryo comes into being. All this has been told to you; what more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ākhyātam etad bhavatā garbhaḥ saṃjāyate yathā yathā jātas tu puruṣaḥ prapadyati tad ucyatām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You have told how the embryo comes to be; now let it be said how, once born, a man fares onward.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca āsannamātraḥ satataṃ tair bhūtair abhibhūyate vipramuktaś ca tair bhūtaiḥ punar yāty aparāṃ gatim sa tu bhūtasamāyuktaḥ prāpnute jīva eva ha
english: Bṛhaspati said: No sooner has it drawn near than it is constantly overpowered by those elements; and when released from those elements it passes again to another state—yet still it is joined with the elements that the living soul attains.

sanskrit: tato 'sya karma paśyanti śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham devatāḥ pañcabhūtasthāḥ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: Then the deities seated in the five elements watch over its deeds, whether fair or foul. What more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca tvagasthimāṃsam utsṛjya taiś ca bhūtair vivarjitaḥ jīvaḥ sa bhagavan kvasthaḥ sukhaduḥkhe samaśnute
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Casting off skin, bone, and flesh, and forsaken by those elements, where, O lord, does that living soul abide while it tastes of pleasure and pain?

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca jīvo dharmasamāyuktaḥ śīghraṃ retastvam āgataḥ strīṇāṃ puṣpaṃ samāsādya sūte kālena bhārata
english: Bṛhaspati said: The living soul, joined with righteousness, swiftly comes into the state of seed and, reaching the flowering of women, is brought to birth in time, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yamasya puruṣaiḥ kleśaṃ yamasya puruṣair vadham duḥkhaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ ca naraḥ kleśaṃ ca vindati
english: Torment at the hands of Yama's servants, slaughter at the hands of Yama's servants, sorrow, the wheel of transmigration, and affliction—these the man finds.

sanskrit: ihaloke ca sa prāṇī janmaprabhṛti pārthiva svakṛtaṃ karma vai bhuṅkte dharmasya phalam āśritaḥ
english: And in this world that living being, from birth onward, O king, reaps the deeds it has itself wrought, resting upon the fruit of righteousness.

sanskrit: yadi dharmaṃ yathāśakti janmaprabhṛti sevate tataḥ sa puruṣo bhūtvā sevate nityadā sukham
english: If from birth onward he practices righteousness to the best of his power, then, becoming a man, he ever after enjoys happiness.

sanskrit: athāntarā tu dharmasya adharmam upasevate sukhasyānantaraṃ duḥkhaṃ sa jīvo 'py adhigacchati
english: But if in the midst of righteousness he turns to practice unrighteousness, then that living soul attains, hard upon its happiness, to sorrow.
